front: TC085: What is the minimum viable move?
back: I asked too many things at once. One question: what is the main part?

front: TC085: What is the core sequence?
back: Stack: notice you are about to ask several questions. -> Reset: "Let me make that one question." -> One anchor: ask the single question that best opens the next useful answer. -> Wait: leave room for the answer without adding a second prompt. -> Follow: choose any later follow-up from what they actually said. -> In one sentence: "I have a few questions, but one first: what happened first?".

front: TC085: What is the field tip?
back: One question mark per turn is the default.

front: TC085: What is the strong version of: "Why did that happen? Who said what? Did you push back? What are you going to do?"?
back: "I am curious about a few things, but one question first: what happened first?"

front: TC085: What is the strong version of: Ask the next prepared question the moment they pause.?
back: "So the first issue was timing, not intent. What happened after that?"

front: TC085: What is the strong version of: Send one message with five asks and expect a clean reply.?
back: "Priority question: can you confirm the deadline? The rest can wait."

front: TC085: What is better than: "Why? What did they say? And then what? What will you do?"?
TC085: What is better than: "Why did you do that? Why didn't you check? Why now?"?
back: "I do not want to cross-examine you. What felt unfair?"

front: TC085: What is better than: Four questions, and only "...what are you going to do?" gets answered.?
back: Ask one question so there is nothing to triage.

front: TC085: What are signs it is working?
back: The person answers with more detail and less guardedness. They choose their own sequence and volunteer context. Their pace slows, their voice steadies, or their body language opens. They answer the question you actually asked rather than skipping around. They lean in and share more than you asked for. Their tone relaxes and they speak more freely.

front: TC085: When should you avoid this technique?
back: A formal checklist, safety protocol, emergency triage or compliance script requires a specific sequence. The other person has clearly asked for a list of questions in advance.

front: TC085: What is the best recovery line?
back: That came out like an interrogation. I am going to slow down and just listen.
